docs.title: Dexterous Hand SDK documentation
docs.text: Explore Python hand interfaces and an in-memory mock for joint commands, joint states, named grasp data and canned teleoperation frames. This documentation describes the public SDK commit 17d8768affe743e9f997f1df5b100ea782ee5526.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Follow source setup.
  2. Run the first mock example.
  3. Explore joint control, grasp sequences and the Hand API.

The mock stores numbers in memory. It does not simulate contact, force, collisions or device dynamics. Linkerbot and OmniHand adapters reject unsupported hardware operations before transport I/O. The current SDK supplies no physical emergency-stop implementation.

class HandDriver(ABC):
    """Minimal interface implemented by vendor-specific drivers."""

    @abstractmethod
    def connect(self) -> None:
        """Open communication with the hand."""

    @abstractmethod
    def disconnect(self) -> None:
        """Close communication with the hand."""

    @abstractmethod
    def read_joints(self) -> list[JointState]:
        """Return the current joint states."""

    @abstractmethod
    def command_positions(self, positions_rad: dict[str, float]) -> None:
        """Command target joint positions in radians."""

    @abstractmethod
    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Request backend-specific stopping behavior.

        The in-memory mock has no physical action. Unsupported vendor adapters
        raise NotImplementedError. This interface does not guarantee a physical
        emergency stop.
        """

Bases: HandDriver

In-memory driver for tests, demos, and documentation examples.

Source code in dexterous_hand/driver.py 
class MockHandDriver(HandDriver):
    """In-memory driver for tests, demos, and documentation examples."""

    def __init__(self, joint_names: list[str]) -> None:
        self._connected = False
        self._positions = {name: 0.0 for name in joint_names}

    def connect(self) -> None:
        self._connected = True

    def disconnect(self) -> None:
        self._connected = False

    def read_joints(self) -> list[JointState]:
        self._require_connected()
        return [JointState(name=name, position_rad=value) for name, value in self._positions.items()]

    def command_positions(self, positions_rad: dict[str, float]) -> None:
        self._require_connected()
        unknown = set(positions_rad) - set(self._positions)
        if unknown:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown joints: {sorted(unknown)}")
        self._positions.update(positions_rad)

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Check mock connection state without any physical action."""
        self._require_connected()

    def _require_connected(self) -> None:
        if not self._connected:
            raise RuntimeError("Driver is not connected")

A named finger with ordered joints and safety limits.

Source code in dexterous_hand/finger.py 
@dataclass
class Finger:
    """A named finger with ordered joints and safety limits."""

    name: str
    joint_names: list[str]
    lower_limits_rad: list[float]
    upper_limits_rad: list[float]

    def validate_positions(self, positions_rad: list[float]) -> None:
        """Validate joint positions against configured limits."""
        if len(positions_rad) != len(self.joint_names):
            msg = f"{self.name} expected {len(self.joint_names)} joints, got {len(positions_rad)}"
            raise ValueError(msg)

        for joint, value, lower, upper in zip(
            self.joint_names, positions_rad, self.lower_limits_rad, self.upper_limits_rad
        ):
            if value < lower or value > upper:
                msg = f"{joint} position {value:.3f} rad outside [{lower:.3f}, {upper:.3f}]"
                raise ValueError(msg)

User-facing API for commanding a dexterous hand.

Source code in dexterous_hand/hand.py 
class Hand:
    """User-facing API for commanding a dexterous hand."""

    def __init__(self, driver: HandDriver, grasp_library: GraspLibrary | None = None) -> None:
        self.driver = driver
        self.grasps = grasp_library or GraspLibrary()

    @classmethod
    def mock(cls) -> Hand:
        """Create a mock hand suitable for examples and tests."""
        driver = MockHandDriver(DEFAULT_JOINTS)
        driver.connect()
        return cls(driver)

    def read_joints(self) -> list[JointState]:
        """Read current joint states."""
        return self.driver.read_joints()

    def move_joints(self, positions_rad: dict[str, float]) -> None:
        """Move joints to target positions."""
        self.driver.command_positions(positions_rad)

    def move_to_grasp(self, grasp_name: str) -> None:
        """Move to a named grasp pose."""
        pose = self.grasps.get(grasp_name)
        self.move_joints(pose.joint_positions_rad)

    def open(self) -> None:
        """Request zero targets for the backend's reported joints.

        The mock resets stored positions; unsupported vendor adapters raise
        NotImplementedError without reading or commanding a physical device.
        """
        joints = {state.name: 0.0 for state in self.read_joints()}
        self.move_joints(joints)

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Request the backend-specific stop operation.

        The in-memory mock performs no physical action. Unsupported vendor
        adapters raise NotImplementedError; this API provides no emergency-stop
        guarantee for a physical device.
        """
        self.driver.stop()

docs.title: Learning exercises
docs.text: The offline examples can be used to explore the distinction between an interface, an implementation and evidence of a physical result.

docs.title: Suggested exercises
docs.text:
1. Inspect Hand.mock() and compare target dictionaries with returned state.
  2. Compare move_to_grasp("open") with open() and explain the different results.
  3. Call Finger.validate_positions() explicitly and distinguish its range check from the general command path.
  4. Supply a canned teleoperation frame and list the additional components a real input adapter would require.

These topics describe possible learning activities; they do not advertise a delivered university course, staffed workshop, hardware qualification or measured learning outcome. Keep exercises offline unless a separate physical-activity review establishes the configuration and responsibilities.

Start with basic control, then grasp sequences.

docs.title: Imitation-learning preparation
docs.text: A proposed imitation-learning experiment needs a defined observation/action representation, timing and task context. Data collection, training and policy evaluation are different pieces of work, each needing explicit source and version records.

docs.title: Current interface examples
docs.text:
TeleoperationFrame can hold supplied joint targets. It does not record human demonstrations, synchronize cameras/sensors, manage dataset permissions or load/train a policy. The RL demo entry point prints an integration instruction; no trained model or inference implementation is supplied there.

Before using a collected dataset, establish provenance, permitted uses and the applicable privacy/workflow requirements. Before making transfer claims, evaluate the exact policy, embodiment mapping and target task. No ACT/Diffusion Policy compatibility, distribution service or automatic retargeting result is established by the current SDK.

Use canned frames for an offline interface exercise and training-data concepts for candidate metadata questions.

docs.title: Research experiments
docs.text: The in-memory SDK can support small software exercises: inspect a target dictionary, compare returned joint objects, test handling of unknown names, or separate supplied commands from an input adapter. These are interface experiments, not measured manipulation performance.

docs.title: Designing an evaluation
docs.text:
State the task, chosen hardware/model, software revision, observation/action representation and success measure. Keep generated mock values separate from captured device data. A reproducible result needs the actual environment and evidence for the behavior being measured.

The current source does not establish tactile sensing, calibrated kinematics, object grasp success, synchronized RGB-D recording or a complete research platform. No hardware/arm/model performance or support service follows from these examples. See training-data concepts and simulation questions for the relevant boundaries.

docs.title: Teleoperation integration planning
docs.text: The public source does not establish a working glove-to-hand rig. read_glove_frame() is unimplemented, and the ROS teleoperation node currently logs a startup message without implementing a live subscription/mapping loop.

docs.title: Plan the boundaries before connecting devices
docs.text:
Specify the input device/interface, coordinate and unit conventions, timestamp behavior, mapping/calibration method, output backend and response to missing or invalid data. A physical setup also needs exact manufacturer documentation and configuration-specific engineering/safety review.

Treat captured human or facility information according to a separately defined collection and permitted-use scope. None of those responsibilities is solved by the TeleoperationFrame.source label.

The canned Python tutorial demonstrates only applying supplied numbers to a mock. It is a useful starting interface example, not evidence of a calibrated 1:1 rig, live recording pipeline or supported installation service.

docs.title: Current in-memory behavior
docs.text:
Hand.move_joints() forwards a dictionary of position targets to its backend. MockHandDriver rejects unknown joint names and updates its stored values immediately. It has no physical trajectory, velocity controller, force feedback or timing model.

Hand.move_to_grasp(name) looks up a target dictionary and forwards it. Hand.open() requests zero targets for the backend's reported joints. The open grasp entry is different: its empty target dictionary leaves existing mock values unchanged.

docs.title: Validation and stopping
docs.text:
The separate Finger.validate_positions() method checks caller-provided values against configured ranges. The general hand command path does not promise to perform that check. Software ranges are not evidence of collision-free or safe physical motion.

Hand.stop() requests backend-specific behavior. In the mock it has no physical action; unsupported vendor adapters raise NotImplementedError. It is not an implemented physical emergency stop. See safety scope.

No physical position, velocity, effort or impedance-control mode is established by the mock example. A future backend needs explicit implementation and its own validation.

docs.title: Grasp vocabulary and mock target sets
docs.text: Power and precision grasps provide a useful vocabulary for discussing manipulation. A power grasp emphasizes broad support/contact, while a precision grasp emphasizes more localized finger contact. This vocabulary does not establish the result of a physical experiment.

docs.title: The source library
docs.text:
The pinned GraspLibrary.default_poses() contains nine primary entries and three compatibility entries (open, pinch, cylindrical), twelve entries total. The target dictionaries below are software example values in radians, not calibrated hardware poses or safe object-handling instructions.

Entry Stored targets relaxed_open thumb_flex=0.08, index_flex=0.08, middle_flex=0.08, ring_flex=0.08, little_flex=0.08 precision_pinch thumb_flex=0.65, index_flex=0.7, middle_flex=0.12, ring_flex=0.08, little_flex=0.08 tripod thumb_flex=0.7, index_flex=0.65, middle_flex=0.62, ring_flex=0.18, little_flex=0.18 lateral_pinch thumb_flex=0.72, index_flex=0.38, middle_flex=0.22, ring_flex=0.18, little_flex=0.18 index_point thumb_flex=0.42, index_flex=0, middle_flex=0.82, ring_flex=0.84, little_flex=0.86 cylindrical_power thumb_flex=0.55, index_flex=0.9, middle_flex=0.9, ring_flex=0.9, little_flex=0.9 spherical_power thumb_flex=0.62, index_flex=0.78, middle_flex=0.82, ring_flex=0.78, little_flex=0.72 hook thumb_flex=0.05, index_flex=1.05, middle_flex=1.08, ring_flex=1.08, little_flex=1.02 platform thumb_flex=0.18, index_flex=0.05, middle_flex=0.05, ring_flex=0.05, little_flex=0.05 open Empty dictionary; leaves existing mock values unchanged pinch thumb_flex=0.65, index_flex=0.7, middle_flex=0.12, ring_flex=0.08, little_flex=0.08 cylindrical thumb_flex=0.55, index_flex=0.9, middle_flex=0.9, ring_flex=0.9, little_flex=0.9

pinch has the same targets as precision_pinch; cylindrical has the same targets as cylindrical_power. Despite its historical name, open does not map to relaxed_open: it carries {}. Use Hand.open() when a mock exercise needs zero targets.

docs.title: Inspecting and customizing values
docs.text:
from dexterous_hand import Hand
from dexterous_hand.grasp_library import GraspPose

hand = Hand.mock()
pose = hand.grasps.get("tripod")
print(pose.joint_positions_rad)
custom = GraspPose("custom", {"index_flex": 0.3}, "Mock exercise")
hand.move_joints(custom.joint_positions_rad)

GraspPose describes a named target dictionary. It does not add force control, object sensing or geometry validation. Continue with the sequence tutorial.

docs.title: Hand and joint data model
docs.text: Hand.mock() uses the software joint names thumb_flex, index_flex, middle_flex, ring_flex and little_flex. These five names do not describe the full kinematic structure or degrees of freedom of any named hardware product.

docs.title: State and commands
docs.text: JointState contains name, position_rad, velocity_rad_s and effort_nm. The mock returns stored position values; velocity and effort remain their default zero values. They are not sensor measurements. A position command is a dictionary mapping known joint names to values in radians; unknown names raise KeyError in the mock.

docs.title: Configured range checks
docs.text:
Finger holds ordered joint names and lower/upper ranges. Its validate_positions() checks the supplied list length and values against those configured ranges. That method is separate from Hand.move_joints(); the mock command path does not automatically call it. These checks do not establish collision avoidance, physical joint protection or a safety-rated controller.

See the Finger API and control behavior for the exact software interfaces.

docs.title: Safety scope
docs.text: The current Python reference SDK and its mock tests do not qualify a physical hand, robot controller or installation for operation.

docs.title: What software operations mean
docs.text:
• Hand.stop() is a backend request. The mock performs no physical action; unsupported vendor operations raise NotImplementedError. It does not provide a physical emergency-stop function.
  • Finger.validate_positions() checks a list against configured numeric ranges when called explicitly. It does not prove collision avoidance, safe contact or protection from physical harm.
  • Mock positions are stored values, not sensed motion or a physical simulation.

docs.title: Before any physical work
docs.text:
A future hardware integration needs exact manufacturer instructions and a configuration-specific engineering and safety review, including the actual equipment stopping functions and responsibility boundaries. These documentation pages cannot supply missing controller, wiring, mounting, calibration or conformity evidence.

For an immediate equipment risk, follow the equipment manufacturer's emergency and safety procedures; email is not an emergency channel. Suspected software vulnerabilities or unsafe behavior can be reported privately to info@stonedrum.co. No response or fix timeline is promised here.

Use the offline example to inspect software behavior without connecting hardware.

docs.title: Training-data concepts
docs.text: A manipulation dataset can describe observations, actions, timestamps and the context in which they were collected. For a proposed dataset, useful fields include sensor/calibration metadata, joint naming and units, task boundaries, outcomes and provenance or permitted-use records.

docs.title: What the current SDK establishes
docs.text:
The public SDK contains hand/joint interfaces and supplied teleoperation frames. It does not include a dexterous_hand.data module, a synchronized recording pipeline, a dataset loader or a demonstrated policy-training/transfer system. A common command dictionary does not eliminate retargeting between different hardware or embodiments.

The in-memory mock does not provide measured tactile feedback, RGB-D synchronization or physical state-action trajectories. Mock values should be labeled as generated software examples rather than captured device data.

docs.title: Future data work
docs.text: Any proposed collection, processing or distribution needs its own scope, source/provenance, permissions, privacy and technical validation. This page makes no GDPR compliance guarantee, dataset availability or partner-distribution claim, release date or early-access offer. Questions about a possible project can go to info@stonedrum.co, without implying an existing data service.

docs.title: Container source status
docs.text:
The SDK includes docker/Dockerfile and docker/docker-compose.yml. The Dockerfile starts from ros:humble-ros-base, adds pip/colcon tooling, copies the SDK and installs its development extras. The Compose file describes a development service with the repository mounted as a volume.

These source files are not proof of a successful image build, an available image registry, or a preinstalled MoveIt/MuJoCo environment. This Docs repair did not build or run the container, and the Python mock checks do not establish container/device compatibility.

Before using a container as reproducible evidence, record the actual base-image digest, dependency resolution, build result, runtime environment and tested behavior. Hardware access and ROS networking require their own configuration-specific review. Use the standalone mock source setup for the smaller offline example.

docs.title: Timing and performance scope
docs.text: The current reference mock stores values in a dictionary; it is not a real-time controller. A ROS source timer period or requested loop frequency is not a measured end-to-end latency, deadline or hardware control rate.

docs.title: Define a measurement before tuning
docs.text:
For a future timing experiment, identify the hardware/software versions, input/output points, clock/timestamp conventions, workload and error/deadline measure. Report observed distributions and conditions rather than inferring performance from a configuration value.

No greater-than-500Hz impedance-control result, real-time-kernel requirement, serial-buffer tuning or safe physical operating configuration is established here. The previous generic tuning instructions are not retained as a device procedure. See ROS source status for what the publisher actually implements.

docs.title: Premier exemple en mémoire
docs.text:
Après la préparation des sources, lancez cet exemple depuis le répertoire du SDK fixé au commit 17d8768affe743e9f997f1df5b100ea782ee5526 :

PYTHONPATH=. python3 - <<'PYTHON'
from dexterous_hand import Hand

hand = Hand.mock()
hand.move_joints({"thumb_flex": 0.25, "index_flex": 0.4})
for state in hand.read_joints():
    print(f"{state.name}: {state.position_rad:.2f} rad")
hand.open()
hand.stop()
PYTHON

Sortie attendue :

thumb_flex: 0.25 rad
index_flex: 0.40 rad
middle_flex: 0.00 rad
ring_flex: 0.00 rad
little_flex: 0.00 rad

Hand.mock() conserve cinq positions en mémoire. move_joints() modifie les valeurs indiquées et read_joints() renvoie cet état logiciel. open() demande des cibles nulles pour les articulations déclarées. stop() ne réalise aucune action physique dans ce backend.

Cet exemple ne commande aucun appareil et ne simule ni contact, ni collision, ni dynamique. Les adaptateurs matériels actuels refusent les opérations non prises en charge avec NotImplementedError avant toute communication. Un changement de constructeur ne fournit donc pas une intégration matérielle. Le SDK ne fournit pas de fonction d'arrêt d'urgence physique validée.

docs.title: Concepts de données d'entraînement
docs.text: Un jeu de données de manipulation peut décrire des observations, des actions, des horodatages et le contexte de leur collecte. Les métadonnées utiles comprennent les unités, les noms d'articulations, la calibration, les limites de tâche, les résultats et les informations de provenance ou d'utilisation autorisée.

docs.title: Portée actuelle du SDK
docs.text:
Les interfaces publiques décrivent des articulations et des trames de commande fournies par l'appelant. Elles ne comprennent pas de module dexterous_hand.data, d'enregistreur synchronisé, de chargeur de données ou de système démontré d'apprentissage et de transfert de politique. Une interface commune ne supprime pas le travail de retargeting entre matériels différents.

Les valeurs du mock sont des exemples logiciels, et non des mesures tactiles, des trajectoires physiques ou des flux RGB-D synchronisés.

docs.title: Projet de collecte ou de distribution
docs.text:
Un tel projet exige sa propre définition de périmètre, sa provenance, ses autorisations, ses exigences de confidentialité et sa validation technique. Cette page ne garantit aucune conformité au RGPD et n'annonce ni jeu de données, ni distribution de données partenaires, ni date de livraison ou accès anticipé.

Les questions sur un projet éventuel peuvent être envoyées à info@stonedrum.co, sans que cela établisse un service de données existant.

docs.title: Que peut-on utiliser sans matériel ?
docs.text: Hand.mock() conserve cinq positions articulaires logicielles. Le premier exemple montre les commandes et les valeurs retournées ; il ne simule pas le contact et ne prouve pas le comportement d'un appareil.

docs.title: Peut-on remplacer le mock par une main physique ?
docs.text: Les adaptateurs Linkerbot/OmniHand actuels refusent les opérations non prises en charge avant toute communication. Un changement de constructeur ne crée pas de pilote fonctionnel. Hand.stop() n'est pas une fonction d'arrêt d'urgence physique implémentée.

docs.title: Quels environnements ont été vérifiés ?
docs.text: Les résultats locaux enregistrés couvrent Python3.11/3.12 ; la CI de la PR corrective a réussi sur Python3.11. Cela ne valide pas tous les systèmes, versions déclarées, distributions ROS, images Docker, configurations MoveIt ou modèles MuJoCo.

docs.title: Combien de poses sont décrites ?
docs.text: Neuf ensembles de cibles principaux et trois entrées de compatibilité. open contient un dictionnaire vide et ne correspond pas à relaxed_open. Hand.open() est une méthode distincte qui demande des cibles nulles.

docs.title: Existe-t-il une lecture de gant ou un service de données ?
docs.text: La lecture de gant n'est pas implémentée dans le contrôleur et l'exemple applique une trame prédéfinie. La page données d'entraînement n'annonce aucun service, jeu de données, calendrier ou garantie de conformité.

docs.title: Comment poser une question ?
docs.text: Utilisez les Issues du SDK pour un problème reproductible et expurgé. Discussions n'est pas activé. Envoyez les rapports sensibles en privé à info@stonedrum.co. Aucun délai de réponse, SLA, service de support ou statut de conformité matérielle n'est promis ici.

docs.title: Préparer les sources
docs.text:
Utilisez les sources publiques du SDK sans supposer la disponibilité d'un paquet sur un registre :

git clone https://github.com/stonedrum-robotics/dexterous-hand-sdk.git
cd dexterous-hand-sdk
git checkout 17d8768affe743e9f997f1df5b100ea782ee5526

Depuis ce répertoire, le premier exemple en mémoire importe le paquet situé à la racine avec PYTHONPATH=.. Aucun appareil ni environnement ROS n'est nécessaire pour cet exemple.

Le projet déclare Python >=3.10. Les vérifications locales enregistrées couvrent Python3.11 et3.12 ; la CI de la PR corrective a réussi sur Python3.11. Cela ne démontre pas une compatibilité testée pour tous les systèmes, toutes les versions déclarées de Python ou les distributions ROS.

Pour développer le SDK dans un environnement virtuel, python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" installe les dépendances déclarées dans pyproject.toml. L'installation et ses dépendances doivent être vérifiées dans l'environnement choisi. ROS, Docker, MoveIt et MuJoCo ont leurs propres besoins et ne sont pas validés par le simple exemple Python.

docs.title: First mock joint update
docs.text:
After source setup, run from the pinned SDK directory:

PYTHONPATH=. python3 - <<'PYTHON'
from dexterous_hand import Hand

hand = Hand.mock()
hand.move_joints({"thumb_flex": 0.25, "index_flex": 0.4})
for state in hand.read_joints():
    print(f"{state.name}: {state.position_rad:.2f} rad")
hand.open()
hand.stop()
PYTHON

Expected joint-state output:

thumb_flex: 0.25 rad
index_flex: 0.40 rad
middle_flex: 0.00 rad
ring_flex: 0.00 rad
little_flex: 0.00 rad

Hand.mock() starts with five stored zero positions. move_joints() updates the named entries, and read_joints() returns their software state. open() requests zero targets for the reported joints. stop() checks the mock connection and performs no physical action.

This example neither moves a device nor simulates one. Swapping a constructor does not provide a working hardware integration: current vendor adapters reject unsupported operations. See hardware setup status.

docs.title: Hardware setup status
docs.text: The published SDK has no working vendor hardware driver. There is no HardwareHandDriver class in dexterous_hand.driver; Linkerbot and OmniHand adapter operations raise NotImplementedError before transport I/O. This page therefore supplies no power-on, pinout, wiring or first-motion procedure.

docs.title: Information needed for a future integration
docs.text:
Record the exact manufacturer, product variant, controller and firmware. Obtain their corresponding manufacturer documentation for electrical ratings, connectors, protocol, mounting and emergency-stop behavior. Assign a configuration-specific engineering and safety review before defining any physical test.

Those facts cannot be inferred from a generic Python interface, a product name or a placeholder value. Stonedrum's published mock code does not establish a conformity assessment, responsibility for a manufacturer's documentation, or device compatibility.

Continue with offline joint updates. Preliminary hardware resource notes are investigation inputs, not commissioning clearance.

docs.title: Source setup
docs.text:
These instructions use the public SDK source rather than assuming a published package registry entry.

git clone https://github.com/stonedrum-robotics/dexterous-hand-sdk.git
cd dexterous-hand-sdk
git checkout 17d8768affe743e9f997f1df5b100ea782ee5526

From that directory, the small mock example can import the root package through PYTHONPATH=.; see first movement. It does not need a device or a ROS installation.

docs.title: Environment evidence
docs.text:
The project declares Python >=3.10. Recorded local checks cover Python 3.11 and 3.12; that evidence does not establish a tested operating-system matrix or a Python 3.10 pass. The correction PR's hosted CI ran Ruff, mypy and pytest on Python 3.11.

For SDK development, use a virtual environment and the dependencies declared in pyproject.toml; python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" installs those dependencies. The editable-install path and downloaded dependency set need their own environment-specific validation. The mock examples use standard-library source interfaces; no package launch or dependency cleanup is implied.

ROS 2 and Docker have separate source status. They are not prerequisites for the Python mock and are not verified by its tests.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A hand interface gives application code names for joint targets and states. In this SDK, Hand delegates operations to a backend implementing HandDriver; Hand.mock() connects a five-joint in-memory backend.

docs.title: What the current source provides
docs.text:
• Stored joint positions and JointState objects.
  • Nine primary grasp target sets and three compatibility entries.
  • A frame object and controller for applying supplied joint targets.
  • Unsupported vendor adapter classes that raise NotImplementedError for hardware operations.

The default joint list is a software example, not a model of a named manufacturer's complete hand. A shared Python interface does not make mock and hardware behavior equivalent or establish interchangeability.

docs.title: Choosing a starting point
docs.text: Use first movement for a small offline example. Read hand model for field definitions and safety scope for the limits of software checks. The ROS 2 and simulation sections describe their own incomplete integration status; no supported multi-platform or physical-device matrix is claimed here.

docs.title: Accessory evaluation
docs.text: An integration may require power, interface, mounting, cabling and instrumentation components. Their selection depends on the exact hardware and site configuration, not on the Python mock's joint names.

docs.title: Record before selecting parts
docs.text:
For each proposed component, record the manufacturer/part revision, required function, mating interfaces, electrical/mechanical limits and source of those limits. Treat power supplies, bus adapters and mounting hardware as separate engineering choices that require configuration-specific review.

The preliminary accessory list is a starting point for investigation. It does not establish exact parts, availability, safe wiring, qualified fit or an orderable Stonedrum bundle. No operating or emergency-cutoff procedure is supplied here.

For a scoped component enquiry, use info@stonedrum.co. A contact route does not promise supply, lead time, installation or support.

docs.title: EG Glove integration questions
docs.text: The EG Glove is referenced as external capture hardware. This documentation does not establish its manufacturer identity, precise product variant, sensor performance, wireless protocol or compatibility with a Stonedrum SDK integration.

docs.title: Current Python behavior
docs.text: TeleoperationFrame holds supplied joint targets and a source label. TeleoperationController.apply_frame() forwards nonempty targets to a Hand. read_glove_frame() raises NotImplementedError; there is no live glove reader, automatic calibration or demonstrated 1:1 hand mapping in this path.

docs.title: Before a device integration
docs.text:
Identify the manufacturer and exact hardware/software revision, obtain its interface and calibration documentation, then define coordinate conventions, units, timestamp behavior and missing-data handling. Captured human or facility data also needs its own collection and permitted-use scope.

No generic calibration routine or device operating procedure is supplied here. The canned frame tutorial shows the software interface without connecting a glove.

docs.text: This route records integration questions rather than a validated Franka Panda / FR3/hand setup. The published SDK supplies no working vendor hand driver and no evidence of a commissioned combined arm-hand system.

An arm controller, mounting adapter, hand controller and application each have configuration-specific constraints. Record their exact models/revisions, manufacturer instructions, coordinate frames, load information, communications and stopping/responsibility boundaries before proposing physical work.

The existence of a flange standard or a generic ROS launch structure does not establish fit, electrical compatibility, collision geometry or a supported combined planning group. A qualified configuration-specific review is needed for those questions.

docs.title: Launch file source status
docs.text: The repository installs launch/hand.launch.py. It creates one hand_node process named dexterous_hand and declares a launch argument named mock with default true.

docs.title: Important distinction
docs.text:
The node parameters in this file contain the literal {"mock": True}; the launch argument is not wired through LaunchConfiguration. Separately, HandNode directly constructs Hand.mock() and does not read a backend parameter. Setting mock:=false does not turn this source into a hardware driver.

config/default.yaml contains mock, publishing-rate and joint-name values, but the inspected launch file does not load that YAML file and the node does not declare/read those parameters. Do not infer a configurable runtime from installed files alone.

This page replaces the former hardware-launch recipe with an explanation of actual source behavior. A working ROS launch/build environment and any future configuration changes require separate validation; none were executed during this documentation repair.

docs.title: ROS 2 node source status
docs.text:
The following descriptions refer to the SDK commit named on the home page; they are static source observations, not a successful ROS runtime demonstration.

Source class Implemented behavior HandNode Constructs Hand.mock(), creates a publisher on relative topic joint_states with depth10, and a0.02-second timer calling publish_joint_states() TeleoperationNode Initializes a node and logs a startup message; no input subscription or mapping loop GraspActionServer Initializes a node and logs a placeholder message; no action server implementation

HandNode populates names, positions, velocities and efforts from mock JointState values. That does not make them measured device telemetry or establish achieved publishing frequency.

These files guard optional ROS imports; their main() functions require rclpy. Configuration keys in a YAML file are not proof that a node reads/applies them. There is no demonstrated hardware-backend selector, live glove controller or physical grasp action in these classes. See topics and services.

docs.title: ROS 2 source overview
docs.text: The SDK repository includes ros2_ws/src/dexterous_hand_ros2/. This is integration source with a different verification boundary from the standalone Python mock. No Humble/Iron/Jazzy compatibility matrix or physical-device support is established by the mock tests.

docs.title: What is present
docs.text:
• HandNode constructs Hand.mock() and publishes software JointState messages from a timer.
  • TeleoperationNode and GraspActionServer start nodes and log messages; they do not implement the documented live command/action pipelines.
  • setup.py declares three console entry points and installs a launch file and configuration file.

The nodes, interfaces and launch file pages describe these exact source boundaries. This repair statically checked those files; it did not run a ROS graph, build with colcon or verify a ROS environment.

Start with the Python mock when exploring joint-state objects. A future ROS runtime evaluation needs its own pinned environment, build/run evidence and interface checks.

docs.title: Actual publication path
docs.text:
HandNode creates a sensor_msgs/msg/JointState publisher using the relative name joint_states. A relative topic may resolve differently under a ROS namespace; this source does not establish the historical /hand/joint_states absolute name.

The callback copies the mock's joint names and stored positions into the message. Velocity/effort use the mock state's default values; they are not readings from hardware. A source timer period is not a measured rate or latency guarantee.

docs.title: Interfaces not implemented here
docs.text:
The inspected node classes do not create the former documented joint-command/glove subscriptions, a grasp action server or command services. The names /hand/joint_commands, /teleop/glove_state and /execute_grasp are therefore not supplied as working endpoints by these classes.

A future interface proposal should specify message types, naming/namespaces, timestamps, units and error behavior, then verify the running graph in a pinned environment. This repair did not execute ROS nodes.

docs.title: Current documented source
docs.text: This repair is based on SDK commit 17d8768affe743e9f997f1df5b100ea782ee5526. The correction makes unsupported vendor operations fail before transport I/O and describes the in-memory mock scope. Its hosted correction-PR CI passed Ruff, mypy and pytest on Python3.11; earlier local checks recorded39 tests on Python3.11/3.12.

docs.title: Historical v0.1.0 label
docs.text:
The inherited Docs called an entry “v0.1.0 — Initial Release,” and pyproject.toml carries version 0.1.0. A version field and historical heading do not establish a published package/tag or prove the former claims of physical L20 control, ROS command subscription, completed integration, robust deployment or broad CI coverage.

The historical source remains preserved in the repository's earlier commit history. Use immutable commits and actual build/test records when stating a release capability. This page does not announce a new package release or retroactively validate the old entry.

docs.title: Contact and reports
docs.text:
For reproducible SDK bugs and documentation problems, use SDK Issues. Include the repository commit, Python/environment version, what you ran and a minimal redacted reproduction. GitHub Discussions are not enabled for these repositories.

Issues are public. Do not include credentials, customer/supplier information, private logs, serial numbers, network addresses or recordings of people/facilities. Suspected vulnerabilities or unsafe software behavior should be reported privately to info@stonedrum.co, with Security: in the subject for security reports.

docs.title: General enquiries
docs.text:
info@stonedrum.co is the general Stonedrum contact for scoped component or integration questions. No acknowledgement/fix timeline, weekly triage, maintenance service, enterprise SLA or hardware support is promised by this page. Email is not an emergency channel.

Stonedrum works across hardware, data and integration in Europe. References to external hardware do not establish Stonedrum manufacture, compatibility, availability or an accepted support contract.

docs.title: What works without hardware?
docs.text: Hand.mock() stores five software joint positions. The first example shows commands and returned state. It does not simulate contact or prove device behavior.

docs.title: Can I switch the mock to a physical hand?
docs.text: The current Linkerbot/OmniHand adapters reject unsupported operations before transport I/O. A working hardware integration is separate work; a constructor swap does not supply it. Hand.stop() is not an implemented physical emergency stop.

docs.title: Which environments have evidence?
docs.text: Recorded local mock checks cover Python3.11 and3.12. The correction PR's hosted CI passed on Python3.11. This does not establish every declared Python/OS version, ROS distribution, Docker image, MoveIt setup or MuJoCo model.

docs.title: How many grasp entries are there?
docs.text: Nine primary target sets plus three compatibility entries. open has empty targets and is not an alias for relaxed_open; see grasp vocabulary.

docs.title: Is live glove input, a data module or a dataset service available here?
docs.text: Those capabilities are not supplied by the current Python interfaces. The canned frame tutorial reads no glove, and training-data concepts announce no dataset, delivery date or compliance guarantee.

docs.title: Where can I ask a question?
docs.text: Use contact and reports. No Discussions route, response SLA, hardware-conformity assurance or staffed support service is established by these Docs.

docs.title: Import errors
docs.text: If dexterous_hand cannot be imported, check that you are using the intended Python interpreter and the pinned SDK source directory, then use PYTHONPATH=. as in source setup. This does not diagnose an unavailable registry package or ROS/container installation.

docs.title: Connection state
docs.text: Hand.mock() connects its backend automatically. A manually constructed MockHandDriver needs connect() before its checked operations; otherwise it raises RuntimeError("Driver is not connected").

docs.title: Names and ranges
docs.text: An unknown target key raises KeyError in the mock. Compare with the default software joint names. Finger.validate_positions() separately raises ValueError for a wrong list length or a value outside its configured bounds. Hand.move_joints() does not automatically invoke that range validator.

docs.title: Unsupported operations
docs.text:
Vendor hardware operations and glove reading deliberately raise NotImplementedError. Do not treat those errors as a cabling problem or bypass them to send unverified commands. ROS node logging/publisher source is not a working grasp action or live teleoperation path.

For a report, include the exact commit and a minimal redacted mock reproduction through contact and reports.

docs.title: Tutorial 1: stored joint values
docs.text:
Use the pinned source setup and run this in the SDK directory with PYTHONPATH=.:

from dexterous_hand import Hand

hand = Hand.mock()
hand.move_joints({"thumb_flex": 0.2, "index_flex": 0.4})
print({s.name: s.position_rad for s in hand.read_joints()})
hand.open()
print([s.position_rad for s in hand.read_joints()])

The first print contains the two supplied values and zero for the remaining joints. The second print is a list of five zeros. There is no physical motion or trajectory; MockHandDriver updates an in-memory dictionary.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
1. Change one known target and compare the returned positions.
  2. Try an unknown joint name and inspect the resulting KeyError.
  3. Construct a Finger with explicit ranges and call validate_positions() separately; compare its errors with the mock command interface.

Do not infer automatic range checking or collision protection from this example. Hand.move_joints() does not call Finger.validate_positions(). Hardware adapters remain unsupported; see control behavior.

docs.title: Tutorial 2: named target sequences
docs.text: The SDK's examples/02_grasp_sequence.py creates Hand.mock() and calls move_to_grasp() for open, pinch, cylindrical, open, printing each name. Those are dictionary lookups and stored position updates; they do not establish a physical grasp.

docs.title: Inspect the state behind the labels
docs.text:
from dexterous_hand import Hand

hand = Hand.mock()
for name in ["open", "pinch", "cylindrical", "open"]:
    hand.move_to_grasp(name)
    print(name, {s.name: s.position_rad for s in hand.read_joints()})

The first open leaves the initially zero values unchanged. The last open also leaves values unchanged, so the cylindrical targets remain stored. Historical example comments saying the sequence ends open are inaccurate. Hand.open() is a different method that requests zero joint targets.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
• Compare open, relaxed_open and Hand.open() using printed software values.
  • Retrieve hand.grasps.get("tripod").joint_positions_rad and inspect the values.
  • Create a GraspPose for a mock exercise and pass its dictionary to move_joints().

The grasp vocabulary gives all nine primary sets and three compatibility entries. Target names and angles are not calibrated object-handling or safe-rest poses for a physical hand.

docs.title: Tutorial 3: supplied teleoperation frames
docs.text:
examples/03_teleoperation_keyboard.py is a canned mock example. It does not read keyboard events or a glove. The useful software boundary is a frame containing supplied target values:

from dexterous_hand import Hand
from dexterous_hand.teleoperation import TeleoperationController, TeleoperationFrame

hand = Hand.mock()
controller = TeleoperationController(hand)
frame = TeleoperationFrame({"thumb_flex": 0.5, "index_flex": 0.5}, "exercise")
controller.apply_frame(frame)
print({s.name: s.position_rad for s in hand.read_joints()})

apply_frame() forwards nonempty target dictionaries. An empty dictionary returns without a command. read_glove_frame() raises NotImplementedError; there is no automatic sensor calibration, coordinate mapping or timing loop in this controller.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text: Supply a second frame and compare values, then supply an empty frame and observe that values remain unchanged. A future live input adapter would need explicit units, coordinate conventions, timestamps and failure handling. This mock exercise does not establish a real rig, data recorder or hardware safety behavior.

docs.title: MoveIt 2 integration questions
docs.text: The current public source does not provide a validated combined arm-hand MoveIt configuration. The demo-apps MoveIt entry point prints setup expectations; it does not launch a supplied planning configuration.

docs.title: What a future planning experiment needs
docs.text:
A planning setup needs a precise robot description, joint conventions/limits, geometry, semantic groups, controllers and a mapping between planning output and an implemented backend. Model provenance and permitted use must be established for the selected files. Collision checking in a model is distinct from qualification of physical operation.

The SDK's mock does not supply a device URDF, collision model or controller bridge. Its five software joint names cannot be used as evidence of a named hand's full kinematics.

Use the ROS source status to inspect existing scaffolding. This page intentionally offers no run-ready arm/hand launch command or SRDF recipe; those require actual configuration and environment validation.

docs.title: MuJoCo integration questions
docs.text: Hand.mock() is not a physics simulator. The demo-apps MuJoCo entry point prints a request for MJCF assets and controller bindings; it does not load a scene or simulate contact.

docs.title: Separate the proposed layers
docs.text:
A future simulation experiment needs a model with geometry, inertial/actuator parameters and joint conventions, an implementation mapping SDK targets/state to that simulator, and a defined validation task. The source/version and reuse terms of any model must also be established.

A shared Python method signature does not establish contact fidelity, sim-to-real transfer or a working MujocoHand adapter. No such adapter or qualified model is supplied by the current mock example.

Begin with stored joint values to understand the interface. A simulation result would need its own pinned scene, controller, software environment and measurements; this documentation repair did not run MuJoCo.
